children: Gold futures fell to ​two-month lows Wednesday as a stronger dollar and U.S. ‌Treasury yields near multiyear highs lowered the appeal of the non-yielding metal.

The U.S. dollar index gained 0.4%, making dollar-denominated ​gold more expensive for holders of other currencies, and benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury ⁠yields climbed to the highest in more than two decades before pulling back.
The 10-year yield slipped to 5.273% after trading as high as 5.361% earlier in the day, its highest intraday level since early 2002.

The minutes from the September 15-16 Federal Open Market Committee meeting showed Fed members acknowledging the need to respond to persistent inflation, with most expecting another rate hike would be necessary before year-end.
"The message is rates are going to continue to be higher for longer, and that's keeping yields and the ​dollar underpinned," Zaner Metals senior metals strategist Peter Grant said in a note.
Earlier gains in oil prices had pressured precious metals prices, given the inflationary implications of higher energy costs.

Meanwhile, official data showed the Peoples Bank of China stepped up its gold ​purchases in September, boosting its gold reserves by 21 tons to 2,196 tons at month's end, marking the Chinese central bank's 23rd consecutive month of purchases.
Fron-month Comex gold (XAUUSD:XUR) for October delivery dropped 1.1% to $4,113.80/oz, its lowest settlement value since August 4, and front-month Comex October silver
slumped 2.1% to $59.899/oz, its lowest close since August 3.

title: Gold futures slump to two-month low on stronger dollar, high yields
